Grisled
GRIZ-ld
adjective
The KJV’s spelling of grizzled, from the Old French grisel, a diminutive of gris, “grey”; hence flecked or patched with grey, of a mottled and mixed colour.

Biblical Definition

Grisled is the KJV’s spelling of grizzled — flecked or patched with grey, of a mottled colour. It occurs in two places only, and both are worth the reader’s eye. The first is Jacob’s account of how the LORD made him rich in Laban’s house against Laban’s will: “I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the rams which leaped upon the cattle were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled” (Gen 31:10). Laban had changed his servant’s wages ten times, and every time God turned the herd to the colour Jacob was owed. The angel says so plainly: “Lift up now thine eyes, and see, all the rams which leap upon the cattle are ringstraked, speckled, and grisled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee” (Gen 31:12). The markings of cattle are in the hand of God: He sees the cheating of a master and answers it in the colour of the lambs. The second place is Zechariah’s vision of the four chariots that come from between two mountains of brass: “in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses” (Zec 6:3); and of the fourth it is said, “the grisled go forth toward the south country” (Zec 6:6). These are the spirits of the heavens, sent to walk to and fro through the earth at the word of the Lord of all the earth. Grey or white or black, they go where He sends them. The same providence that speckled Jacob’s flock drives the chariots of heaven.

Webster 1828 Definition

The KJV’s spelling of grizzled; flecked or streaked with grey, of a mottled and mixed colour.

GRISLED, the KJV spelling of grizzled; grey, or interspersed with grey; of a mixed colour.

From the Old French grisel, a diminutive of gris, “grey.”

It describes the ringstraked and speckled cattle of Jacob’s wages (Gen 31:10).

It describes the horses of Zechariah’s fourth chariot (Zec 6:3).

It occurs in these two places only in all the Scripture.

Key Scripture

Gen 31:10 — "And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived, that I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the rams which leaped upon the cattle were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled."

Gen 31:12 — "And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see, all the rams which leap upon the cattle are ringstraked, speckled, and grisled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee."

Zec 6:3 — "And in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses."

Zec 6:6 — "The black horses which are therein go forth into the north country; and the white go forth after them; and the grisled go forth toward the south country."

Modern Corruption

Not a contested doctrine but an old word for grey-flecked; it recovers a providence that reaches to the colour of a lamb and to the horses of heaven.

expand to see more

The word rebukes a small view of providence. Laban changed his servant’s wages ten times, and each time God changed the flock to match — ringstraked, speckled, grisled, whatever Jacob was owed. The angel gives the reason: “I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.” God is not indifferent to a cheated workman, and He does not wait upon the courts. He answers in the very currency of the fraud, and the defrauder watches his own herd turn against him. Let no man think his master’s dealings beneath heaven’s notice, and let no master think his book-keeping is hidden.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the reach of that same government. The hand that mottled the lambs in Padanaram drives the four chariots out from between the mountains of brass, and the grisled horses go forth toward the south country because the Lord of all the earth has sent them. There is no realm too small for Him and none too great. The believer who trusts God with the nations may safely trust Him with his wages; and the believer who has seen Him keep the wages may safely trust Him with the nations. He that numbers the grey hairs in a lamb’s coat numbers the very hairs of your head.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means grey-flecked, mottled — the KJV’s spelling of grizzled.

expand to see more

Grisled — the KJV’s spelling of grizzled.

From Old French grisel, a diminutive of gris, “grey.”

It denotes a coat flecked or patched with grey, of a mixed colour.

It marks the cattle God gave Jacob against Laban’s fraud (Gen 31:10).

It marks the horses of Zechariah’s fourth chariot (Zec 6:3).

Usage

"The rams were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled — God paid Jacob out of Laban’s own herd."

"I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee: heaven keeps the books of a cheated workman."

"The grisled horses go forth toward the south country at the word of the Lord of all the earth."
